featured.title: Sundar Pichai Just Raised $85 Billion in a Single Week. It's the Largest Tech Equity Offering Ever.
featured.excerpt: Alphabet's oversubscribed capital raise, anchored by a $10 billion Berkshire Hathaway bet, will fund $180 billion in AI infrastructure spending this year alone.
featured.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, in 2023
featured.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai, the IIT Kharagpur alumnus who runs the most consequential AI company in the world, is staking an unprecedented sum on infrastructure that will employ thousands of Indian engineers. Google Cloud's $460 billion backlog means years of enterprise AI work ahead — much of it built and maintained by the Indian talent pipeline that already dominates Google's engineering ranks.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: From Memes to Monarchy: RCB's Dynasty Has Arrived
editorial.excerpt: Royal Challengers Bengaluru retain the IPL title with a five-wicket demolition of Gujarat Titans in Ahmedabad — and a 15-year-old from Sambalpur might just have stolen the entire season.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Used the Shangri-La Dialogue to Talk to Everyone. That Was the Point.
news.excerpt: In Singapore, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh held meetings with US INDOPACOM, NATO's military chief, the Swedish defence ministry, the Netherlands, and Singapore's president — all in 48 hours. India's message: strategic autonomy is not isolation.
news.image_caption: The Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, Asia's premier defence summit
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The US Wants India to Go Nuclear. This Time, the Private Sector Is Leading.
news.excerpt: US Ambassador Sergio Gor says Washington and New Delhi are pushing civil nuclear cooperation to 'new levels' — with private companies, not governments, building the reactors India needs to power its AI ambitions.
news.image_caption: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, who is pushing for a private sector-led civil nuclear partnership with India
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Nine Hundred Tankers Went Dark to Cross the Strait of Hormuz. India Is One of the Countries Paying for Passage.
news.excerpt: Two-thirds of outbound oil tankers are switching off tracking systems to slip through Iran's blockade. Some are paying Tehran up to $2 million per crossing — and India, China, Pakistan, and Japan are among those using the corridor.
news.image_caption: Oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for a fifth of global oil supply
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Delhi Hotel Had No Fire Exit and Too Many Rooms. Twenty-One People Died Inside.
news.excerpt: The Flourish Stay B&B in Malviya Nagar was approved for six rooms but operated more than twenty. Most of the dead were foreign nationals who came to India for medical treatment.
news.image_caption: Firefighters respond to a building fire with emergency vehicles on scene
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and Canada Just Launched a Trade Forum. The Real Prize Is a Free Trade Deal by December.
news.excerpt: Piyush Goyal and Mark Carney are fast-tracking CEPA negotiations that could unlock a $50 billion trade corridor and reshape economic ties for 2.8 million Indian-Canadians.
news.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal led the trade delegation to Canada
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Man Tore the Indian Flag Outside a Texas City Hall. The Video Went Global in Hours.
news.excerpt: The Frisco incident comes as anti-Indian sentiment intensifies in North Dallas, where the Indian-origin population has tripled since 2010. Community leaders say the debate has crossed a line.
news.image_caption: The Indian national tricolor flying in New Delhi
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Almost Missed the World Cup. Then Zee Signed an Eight-Year Deal Ten Days Before Kickoff.
news.excerpt: Zee Entertainment secures FIFA broadcast rights through 2034 for roughly $60 million, ending months of uncertainty and launching the Unite8 Sports network in the process.
news.image_caption: The FIFA World Cup trophy displayed at a tournament event
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The RBI Held Rates. Then It Threw the Rupee a Lifeline India's Bond Market Has Never Seen.
news.excerpt: Capital gains tax scrapped for foreign bond investors, NRI deposit schemes sweetened, and concessional forex swaps extended — all in a single policy announcement aimed at stopping the rupee's slide.
news.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes and coins reflecting the central bank rate decision
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is About to Pay Companies to Process Lithium and Nickel. The Minimum Entry Is 30,000 Tonnes.
news.excerpt: A ₹3,000 crore incentive package for critical mineral processing is imminent, targeting the chokehold China has on India's EV battery supply chain.
news.image_caption: Electric vehicle battery cells on a manufacturing line
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Subhash C Kashyap, the Man Who Defined How India's Parliament Works, Is Dead at 97
news.excerpt: The former Lok Sabha Secretary-General authored over 100 books on constitutional law and served Parliament for nearly four decades, from Nehru's first Lok Sabha to the ninth.
news.image_caption: Subhash C Kashyap, former Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Tim Cook's Final Keynote Is on Monday. Apple Is Betting Everything on AI It Can Run on Your Phone.
news.excerpt: WWDC 2026 will unveil a Siri overhaul powered by Google's Gemini, an edge-AI strategy that prioritises on-device processing, and a bill-splitting feature in Apple Wallet. It is also the last major stage for the CEO who turned Apple into a $3 trillion company.
news.image_caption: Tim Cook, Apple CEO, at a public appearance in March 2026
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Drone Just Hit Oman's Largest Oil Terminal. India's Hormuz Bypass Is No Longer Safe.
news.excerpt: The explosion at Mina al Fahal extends the Middle East conflict beyond the Strait of Hormuz and into the open-ocean infrastructure India was counting on to keep crude flowing.
news.image_caption: Cargo ships docked near oil storage tanks at a coastal port facility
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Reliance's Hiring Has Slowed to a Crawl. AI Is About to Make It Worse.
news.excerpt: India's largest private employer grew headcount by just 4% last year, one quarter of the previous year's pace. At TCS and Infosys, the workforce has already shrunk. The AI squeeze is only beginning.
news.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani at a company event in Mumbai
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: PhysicsWallah Killed Its Lending Plan One Week After Announcing It. The Stock Surged 18%.
news.excerpt: The edtech giant scrapped a ₹120 crore student lending bet after investors revolted — and the market rewarded the U-turn instantly.
news.image_caption: PhysicsWallah co-founder Alakh Pandey built the edtech platform from a YouTube channel
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: New York's State Senate Just Declared August 15 India Independence Day. The Man Behind It Was Adopted From Kolkata.
news.excerpt: Resolution J1935 urges Governor Kathy Hochul to formally recognise India's 79th Independence Day across the state — sponsored by the first Asian American elected to state office from upstate New York.
news.image_caption: The New York State Senate adopted Resolution J1935 recognising India Independence Day
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Buying Oil From Venezuela, Brazil, Angola and Nigeria. The Hormuz Shutdown Forced Its Hand.
news.excerpt: As the Strait of Hormuz enters its fourth month of near-total closure, Indian refiners have quietly built a new supply chain stretching from Latin America to West Africa — a structural shift that may outlast the conflict.
news.image_caption: A crude oil tanker at sea — India's refiners are now sourcing from Latin America and Africa to offset Hormuz losses
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A New Bill Wants to Kill the H-1B Lottery and End OPT. Indian Tech Workers Are in the Crosshairs.
news.excerpt: Republican Chip Roy's American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act would replace the visa lottery with a wage-based system, ban companies that laid off workers from hiring H-1B holders, and abolish the OPT program that hundreds of thousands of Indian students rely on.
news.image_caption: U.S. Representative Chip Roy of Texas, who introduced the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian Court Just Ruled That ChatGPT Is Not an Intermediary. It Is a Creator.
news.excerpt: The Calcutta High Court's classification of generative AI as an 'originator' under the IT Act strips it of safe-harbour protection and opens a legal frontier India has no framework to govern.
news.image_caption: The Calcutta High Court, where Justice Ravi Krishan Kapur issued the landmark AI classification ruling
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Trade Deal With Oman Just Went Live. For 700,000 Gulf Indians, It's More Than Tariffs.
nri-world.excerpt: The India-Oman CEPA, which entered into force on June 1, is Oman's first bilateral trade agreement since the US deal in 2006 — and it includes mobility provisions that could reshape how Indian professionals work in the Gulf.
nri-world.image_caption: Aerial view of Muscat port with ship, cranes, and mountains in the background
nri-world.nri_angle: Nearly 700,000 Indians live in Oman, many in merchant families with roots stretching back two centuries. The CEPA's enhanced mobility provisions — easing entry for accountants, architects, healthcare workers — directly affect the professional class of the Gulf diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Five South Asian Candidates Just Won Georgia Primaries. One Could Become the State's First Sikh Official.
nri-world.excerpt: In a state with 600,000 Asian American residents, Indian and South Asian candidates swept five races in the May 19 primary — including a milestone for the Sikh community that Georgia has never seen.
nri-world.image_caption: The Georgia State Capitol in Atlanta, where newly elected South Asian lawmakers will take their seats
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian and South Asian Americans are building political power in Georgia at an unprecedented pace — from state house seats to a potential lieutenant governorship. The results mark a generational shift in how the diaspora engages with American democracy beyond the coasts.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's $135 Billion Remittance Lifeline Is Under Pressure From Three Directions at Once.
nri-world.excerpt: AI-driven tech layoffs, a $100,000 H-1B visa fee, and a new US remittance levy are squeezing the financial pipeline that covers nearly half of India's trade deficit — and the consequences are about to reach millions of NRI families.
nri-world.image_caption: A currency exchange office window displaying conversion rates in a city centre
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, who now send more money home than Gulf workers, face a triple squeeze: their jobs are being automated, their visas cost more, and their transfers are being taxed. The shift threatens household budgets from Hyderabad to Houston.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: New York's State Senate Just Voted to Recognize August 15 as India Independence Day. The Speeches Said More Than the Resolution.
nri-world.excerpt: Multiple senators spoke about India's civilizational heritage, Gandhi's legacy, and the Indian-American community's contributions — a sign of the diaspora's growing political weight in one of America's most powerful state legislatures.
nri-world.image_caption: The New York State Capitol in Albany, where the Senate adopted Resolution J1935 recognizing India Independence Day
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Half of All Indian Americans Report Discrimination. The Carnegie Survey Puts a Number on What the Community Already Knew.
nri-world.excerpt: The 2026 Indian American Attitudes Survey finds that one in four has been called a slur, 48 per cent regularly encounter racist posts online, and the community's Democratic lean is softening — but not breaking.
nri-world.image_caption: A South Asian couple on a street in the United States
nri-world.nri_angle: The Carnegie IAAS survey is the definitive portrait of where Indian Americans stand in 2026 — navigating discrimination, political realignment and an identity paradox that success alone cannot resolve.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Indian Was Killed at Kuwait Airport. For 8.9 Million Gulf Indians, the War Just Got Personal.
nri-world.excerpt: Iranian drones struck the newly reopened terminal, killing one Indian national and wounding 63 others. India has already evacuated 52,000 from the region.
nri-world.image_caption: Kuwait International Airport terminal building before the June 2026 drone strike
nri-world.nri_angle: The 8.9 million Indians living in the Gulf are caught between the economic necessity of staying and the escalating danger of the US-Iran war. This strike brings the conflict directly to the diaspora's doorstep.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is '99% Done.' The Diaspora Built the Other 99 Per Cent.
nri-world.excerpt: Ambassador Gor says only technical legal language remains. Bilateral trade has grown from $20 billion to $220 billion — much of it on the backs of 5.2 million Indian Americans.
nri-world.image_caption: President Trump with Indian officials during his visit to India
nri-world.nri_angle: The India-US economic relationship was built by the diaspora over three decades. The trade deal formalizes what Indian Americans already made real — and its fine print on investment, trade facilitation and economic security alignment will directly affect NRI entrepreneurs and professionals.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Spirits Just Landed in Canadian Duty-Free. The Diaspora Built the Runway.
nri-world.excerpt: An 'Indian Aisle' now sits inside Toronto Pearson, Vancouver International, and duty-free shops along the Ontario-BC border — the first time Indian-made spirits have entered Canada's travel retail market.
nri-world.image_caption: Interior of Toronto Pearson International Airport Terminal 1, one of the locations hosting the new Indian Aisle
nri-world.nri_angle: The 1.9 million Indo-Canadians who pass through these airports are now the test market for Indian premium spirits in North America. What looks like a retail launch is really a bet on whether the diaspora's cultural tastes can open a commercial channel that did not exist before.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Just Revamped Its OCI Portal for Five Million Cardholders. The Old System Was Built in 2013.
nri-world.excerpt: Amit Shah launched a modernised Overseas Citizen of India platform with auto-fill, in-built payments, and real-time tracking — replacing a portal that processed 2,000 applications a day on decade-old infrastructure.
nri-world.image_caption: Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who inaugurated the revamped OCI portal in New Delhi
nri-world.nri_angle: The OCI card is the primary legal document connecting 5 million diaspora Indians to their homeland. A clunky portal meant lost hours, abandoned applications, and deferred trips. The upgrade matters because it is the bureaucratic front door to India for every NRI who holds one.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: 75,000 Indians Left Britain Last Year. They Were Also the Largest Group Arriving.
nri-world.excerpt: New ONS data shows UK net migration fell to 171,000, its lowest since 2021. Indians dominated every category — arrivals, departures, skilled work extensions, and student visas — exposing a contradiction Britain has not resolved.
nri-world.image_caption: UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, who announced the net migration figures
nri-world.nri_angle: For the 1.8 million-strong Indian diaspora in Britain, the numbers tell a story of a community that is simultaneously the most wanted and the most expendable. Indians fill the NHS, lead skilled worker extensions, and dominate student visas — yet they also lead the exit charts, caught between tightening visa rules and a political climate that treats immigration as a number to be managed down.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A 14-Year-Old From California Just Won the Scripps Spelling Bee. He Spelled 32 Words in 90 Seconds.
nri-world.excerpt: Shrey Parikh shattered the spell-off record, defeated Ishaan Gupta in a lightning round, and extended Indian-American dominance of the most famous vocabulary contest.
nri-world.image_caption: The stage at the Scripps National Spelling Bee in Washington, D.C.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: NRI Investors Are Flooding Into GIFT City. The Numbers Just Tripled in Three Months.
nri-world.excerpt: Retail participation in Gujarat's international financial hub nearly tripled in Q4 FY26, as new mutual fund schemes and lower minimums finally make India's offshore platform accessible to ordinary diaspora investors.
nri-world.image_caption: Aerial view of GIFT City in Gandhinagar, Gujarat
nri-world.nri_angle: GIFT City was built to capture NRI money that currently sits in foreign bank accounts and global equity markets. The tripling of retail participation signals that the diaspora is finally treating it as a serious alternative to investing through US or UK brokerages.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The RBI Held Rates While the Rupee Hit Historic Lows. Here Is What It Means for Every NRI.
markets-finance.excerpt: Repo rate stays at 5.25 per cent for a third straight meeting. The rupee is at 96.72, oil is near $96, and the central bank is betting the Gulf crisis will cool before inflation forces a hike.
markets-finance.image_caption: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra who announced the June 2026 rate decision
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreign Firms Are Using India's IPO Boom to Send $5 Billion Back to HQ. NRI Investors Should Understand Why.
markets-finance.excerpt: Five of six foreign companies that listed Indian units since 2024 raised zero new capital. The IPOs were structured purely as exits. For NRIs holding these stocks or eyeing the next wave, the pattern matters.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's oldest and largest stock exchange
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Alphabet Just Raised $85 Billion by Selling Its Own Stock. If You Own GOOGL, Here Is What That Means.
markets-finance.excerpt: Google's parent company upsized its equity offering to $84.75 billion — the largest stock sale in corporate history — to fund AI data centres. The move cancels buybacks, dilutes shareholders, and signals that the AI spending race has outgrown even Big Tech's enormous cash flows.
markets-finance.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet, has called demand for AI computing power 'unprecedented'
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India and the US Are '99 Per Cent' Done on a Trade Deal. Here Is What It Means for Every NRI.
markets-finance.excerpt: US Ambassador Sergio Gor says the bilateral trade agreement is imminent. Tariffs on Indian goods could drop from 50 to 18 per cent. For NRIs sending money, investing, or running businesses across both countries, the stakes are enormous.
markets-finance.image_caption: India-US bilateral trade negotiations approach their final stages
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Broadcom Just Beat Every Estimate. Its Stock Fell 15 Per Cent Anyway. Here Is What NRI Investors Need to Understand.
markets-finance.excerpt: Record revenue, record margins, record AI bookings — and the worst single-day drop in months. The AI trade is entering a new phase where perfection is not enough.
markets-finance.image_caption: A semiconductor chip — the building block of the AI infrastructure boom
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The RBI Decides on Rates Tomorrow. The Rupee Is at 95.75, Oil Is Near $97, and NRI Money Is Caught in the Middle.
markets-finance.excerpt: Most economists expect a hold at 5.25 per cent, but traders are split on whether a surprise hike could come. What the decision means for remittances, property investments, and equity markets.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai ahead of the June 2026 monetary policy decision
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Scrapped Capital Gains Tax on Foreign Bond Investments. Here Is Why NRIs Should Care.
markets-finance.excerpt: The cabinet approved eliminating the 12.5 per cent tax on government securities as the rupee slides and oil threatens inflation. The RBI decides on rates tomorrow.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: SpaceX Just Set the Price for the Largest IPO in History. Here Is What NRI Investors Need to Know.
markets-finance.excerpt: At $135 a share and a $1.75 trillion valuation, SpaceX's June 12 Nasdaq debut will dwarf every public offering before it. The numbers are extraordinary — and so are the risks.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Oil Is Near $100. The US Just Proposed a 12.5 Per Cent Tariff on India. NRI Investors Face a Dual Shock.
markets-finance.excerpt: Iran hostilities pushed Brent crude to $97.81 on Wednesday while Trump's trade office proposed new forced-labour tariffs on 60 economies — including India at the higher 12.5 per cent rate. Here is what it means for Indian markets and your portfolio.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Microsoft Just Lost Over $200 Billion in Market Value During Its Biggest AI Week of the Year. If You Hold MSFT, Here Is What Is Happening.
markets-finance.excerpt: The stock fell more than 7 per cent across two sessions despite an Nvidia partnership, seven new AI models, an autonomous agent launch, and a quantum computing breakthrough. Wall Street is sending a clear message about the gap between AI announcements and AI earnings.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The OECD Just Warned of the Weakest Growth Since 2008. Oil Is Near $100. A Private Equity Giant Froze Withdrawals. Here Is What It Means for NRI Investors.
markets-finance.excerpt: Three simultaneous shocks — a growth downgrade, a private credit rout, and escalating Gulf hostilities — converged on markets Wednesday. The diaspora's exposure is real.
markets-finance.nri_angle: India imports 85%+ of crude oil — $98 Brent directly hits India's current account deficit and rupee. NRI alternative fund allocations face liquidity risk. US index fund concentration masks weakness.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Broadcom Reports Earnings Today. At $2.25 Trillion, It Is the Biggest AI Chip Test of the Quarter.
markets-finance.excerpt: Wall Street expects $22.1 billion in revenue and $2.40 in adjusted EPS — both records — as the chipmaker's AI business doubles and oil prices push past $97 in the background.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Face Pakistan and China in the U-18 Asia Cup Semifinals Today. Sardar Singh Says His Team Is Ready.
sports.excerpt: The U-18 men take on Pakistan at 3:30 PM IST in Kakamigahara. The women, unbeaten with a 25-0 rout in the group stage, face China at 9:30 AM. Both squads have outscored opponents by a combined 57-7.
sports.image_caption: Sardar Singh, now U-18 men's coach, during his playing days with the Indian hockey team at Kalinga Stadium
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Half a Point Separates First and Second. Norway Chess Will Be Decided in the Final Round Today.
sports.excerpt: Wesley So leads Praggnanandhaa by the thinnest margin. Firouzja is a point behind. Three pairings on Friday will determine who takes home the title and the $100,000 prize.
sports.image_caption: Wesley So, the tournament leader heading into the final round of Norway Chess 2026
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Harmanpreet Will Lead India at a Fifth T20 World Cup. This Time, She Has Nandni Sharma and a Point to Prove.
sports.excerpt: India's 15-player squad for the Women's T20 World Cup in England features a maiden call-up for Chandigarh pacer Nandni Sharma, the return of Yastika Bhatia and Radha Yadav, and a team that has won just three of its last eight T20Is.
sports.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur, captain of India's Women's T20 World Cup squad
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Praggnanandhaa Beats Gukesh for the Third Time in Oslo. He Is Half a Point Behind Wesley So With One Round Left.
sports.excerpt: The 20-year-old Indian grandmaster completed a hat-trick of classical wins over the reigning World Champion at Norway Chess 2026, while Bibisara Assaubayeva clinched the women's title with a round to spare.
sports.image_caption: R. Praggnanandhaa at a chess tournament
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Sixty Countries. Four Hundred Athletes. India Just Turned Yoga Into a Competitive Sport With an Olympic Ambition.
sports.excerpt: The first World Yogasana Championship opened in Ahmedabad on Thursday, with electronic scoring, six age categories, and a clear pitch for Olympic recognition.
sports.image_caption: Athletes performing yogasana during a competitive event
sports.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora in the US, UK, and Canada — where yoga studios outnumber cricket clubs — the World Yogasana Championship reframes a cultural practice they have long practiced recreationally as an internationally competitive sport with Olympic aspirations.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two World No. 1 Rankings. Seventeen Top-10 Finishes Across Twenty Weight Classes. Indian Boxing Has Never Been This Deep.
sports.excerpt: Minakshi Hooda and Jaismine Lamboria both hold the top spot in their divisions. India now features in the top 10 of nine of ten women's and eight of ten men's weight categories.
sports.image_caption: Jaismine Lamboria during an international boxing competition
sports.nri_angle: For NRI fans tracking India's Olympic medal prospects, the rankings signal unprecedented depth across weight classes. With Asian Games seedings in Aichi-Nagoya determined by these standings, Indian boxers enter with two No. 1 seeds and multiple top-three placements.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Beat Carlsen With White. Then He Beat Carlsen With Black. Praggnanandhaa Is Half a Point Behind the Leader With One Round to Go.
sports.excerpt: Only Viswanathan Anand had done it before. The 20-year-old from Chennai now has two classical wins over the world's number one in the same tournament at Norway Chess 2026.
sports.image_caption: R Praggnanandhaa, the 20-year-old Indian grandmaster competing at Norway Chess 2026
sports.nri_angle: Indian chess is in a golden era — Praggnanandhaa becomes only the second Indian after Anand to beat Carlsen twice in one event, while the world champion Gukesh and women's players Divya Deshmukh and Koneru Humpy also compete at Norway Chess.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: They Were Born in Auckland, Doha, Melbourne, and Paris. All Four Trace Their Roots to India. All Four Are Going to the World Cup.
sports.excerpt: Sarpreet Singh, Tahsin Mohammed, Nishan Velupillay, and Samuel Moutoussamy will represent four different nations at the 2026 FIFA World Cup — the largest group of Indian-origin players at a single tournament in history.
sports.image_caption: Sarpreet Singh during training with FC Bayern Munich in 2019
sports.nri_angle: Four players of Indian origin — from Punjab, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Indo-Guadeloupean Tamil roots — represent New Zealand, Qatar, Australia, and DR Congo at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the largest Indian-heritage presence at the tournament since Vikash Dhorasoo in 2006.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: 'In a Family of Four, We All Lived the Same Dream.' KS Bharat Retires From International Cricket at 32.
sports.excerpt: The Visakhapatnam wicketkeeper-batter played seven Tests for India, including the 2023 WTC final at The Oval, before stepping away with an emotional note thanking Kohli, Rohit, and Dravid.
sports.image_caption: A wicketkeeper in action during a cricket test match
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Satwik and Chirag Were Out. Hariharan and Arjun Stepped In. India Has a Second Doubles Pair at the Super 1000 Level.
sports.excerpt: MR Arjun and Hariharan Amsakarunan fought back from a game down to reach the Indonesia Open quarterfinals — a first for any Indian men's doubles pair outside the Satwik-Chirag partnership at a BWF Super 1000 event.
sports.image_caption: Badminton doubles players in action during a professional tournament
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Rights Groups Say NRI Fans Face a 'Climate of Fear' at the World Cup. FIFA Has Not Responded.
sports.excerpt: With the tournament kicking off June 11 across the United States, the Sport and Rights Alliance warns that Trump's immigration crackdown has turned the world's biggest sporting event into a source of anxiety for diaspora fans and travellers on temporary visas.
sports.image_caption: Football fans celebrate in the stands during a major international tournament
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Pant Lost the Vice-Captaincy and the LSG Armband. His Coaches Say the Problem Is Not Leadership. It Is Shot Selection.
sports.excerpt: Ryan ten Doeschate and childhood coach Devender Sharma say India's wicketkeeper must stop forcing horizontal shots and start playing to the match situation. The Afghanistan Test is his proving ground.
sports.image_caption: A cricket wicketkeeper-batter in action during a match
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Sundar Pichai Just Raised $85 Billion in a Single Week. It's the Largest Tech Equity Offering Ever.
technology.excerpt: Alphabet's oversubscribed capital raise, anchored by a $10 billion Berkshire Hathaway bet, will fund $180 billion in AI infrastructure spending this year alone.
technology.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, in 2023
technology.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai, the IIT Kharagpur alumnus who runs the most consequential AI company in the world, is staking an unprecedented sum on infrastructure that will employ thousands of Indian engineers. Google Cloud's $460 billion backlog means years of enterprise AI work ahead — much of it built and maintained by the Indian talent pipeline that already dominates Google's engineering ranks.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Arvind Krishna's IBM Just Partnered With Google Cloud on Agentic AI. The $1 Billion Quantum Grant Helps Too.
technology.excerpt: IBM and Google are building industry-specific AI agents for banking, healthcare, and government — while a Department of Commerce grant will fund America's first quantum chip foundry under IBM's roof.
technology.image_caption: Arvind Krishna, Chairman and CEO of IBM, in 2025
technology.nri_angle: Arvind Krishna, the IIT Kanpur alumnus who has led IBM since 2020, is positioning the company at the centre of two transformational bets — agentic AI and quantum computing. IBM's consulting arm employs tens of thousands of Indian-origin professionals globally, and the new Google Cloud Practice will create substantial demand for engineers who can build enterprise AI agents. For Indian IT professionals at TCS, Infosys, and Wipro watching the consulting landscape shift, IBM's play is both a competitive threat and a career signal: the premium work is moving to AI agent deployment.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks Hit $3 Billion in Quarterly Revenue. AI Is the Reason.
technology.excerpt: The former Google executive's cybersecurity empire posted 31% revenue growth, tripled its AI security customer base, and raised guidance — then watched the stock drop 6%.
technology.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, at TechCrunch Disrupt
technology.nri_angle: Nikesh Arora is the highest-profile Indian-origin CEO in cybersecurity, running a $242 billion company from Santa Clara. His success story — from Uttar Pradesh to Google's chief business officer to Palo Alto Networks CEO — is a template for Indian executives moving beyond traditional software into vertical leadership. The AI security market he is building will require thousands of Indian-origin security engineers and consultants who already dominate the cybersecurity workforce at major enterprises.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: AI Is Now America's Top Excuse for Firing People. The Data Says It Might Not Be Wrong.
technology.excerpt: Challenger data shows 88,000 AI-driven job cuts in five months — already exceeding all of 2025. For Indian H-1B holders, the 60-day clock is ticking louder than ever.
technology.image_caption: Workers at a technology company office
technology.nri_angle: Indians hold 71-73% of H-1B visas. AI-driven layoffs at Meta, Amazon, and Oracle disproportionately affect Indian tech workers who face a 60-day grace period to find new sponsorship or leave the US.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Meta Is Recording How Its Engineers Use Computers. The 30-Minute Bathroom Break Was a Concession.
technology.excerpt: The Model Capability Initiative captures keystrokes, clicks, and screenshots to train AI agents. Employees protested. Zuckerberg called them 'smart people.' Then 8,000 of them got laid off.
technology.image_caption: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, who called his employees 'smart people' whose computer use should train AI models
technology.nri_angle: Meta is one of the largest H-1B employers for Indian engineers. Workers are generating training data for AI while watching colleagues get laid off — and their own immigration status depends on staying employed at the company building their replacement.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Cadence Gave IIT Delhi Its Best Chip Design Tools. India's Talent Pipeline Still Isn't Ready.
technology.excerpt: The new innovation lab puts 200+ industry-grade EDA tools in students' hands. But India needs 85,000 semiconductor engineers by 2030, and most of the ones it has are working in San Jose.
technology.image_caption: A semiconductor circuit board — India is racing to build its chip design talent pipeline
technology.nri_angle: 25-30% of the US semiconductor workforce is Indian-origin. India's chip ambitions depend on this diaspora returning or the domestic pipeline catching up — the Cadence-IIT Delhi lab is a bet on the latter.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Palantir's Google Cloud Deal Has an Indian Architect. So Does the Company.
technology.excerpt: At AIPCon 10, Palantir's Indian-origin Chief Architect Akshay Krishnaswamy brokered the firm's deepest platform partnership yet. CTO Shyam Sankar built the AI engine behind it.
technology.image_caption: Server racks in a modern data centre — the infrastructure Palantir and Google Cloud aim to power with AI
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin leaders hold the two most important technical roles at Palantir — Chief Architect Akshay Krishnaswamy and CTO Shyam Sankar — shaping AI infrastructure used by governments and enterprises worldwide. Accenture, a top Indian-professional employer, is a key Palantir partner.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Five Indian States Crashed Computex. The Chip Supply Chain Noticed.
technology.excerpt: Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh pitched Taiwanese chipmakers at the world's biggest tech expo. One state is betting everything on semiconductor packaging.
technology.image_caption: A semiconductor cleanroom, the kind of facility Indian states are competing to attract
technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian semiconductor professionals work at TSMC, Intel, Qualcomm, AMD, and Micron. India's chip push is creating a realistic return-to-India career path beyond software for the first time, plus investment opportunities in semiconductor manufacturing.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT Now 'Dreams' About You. Its Memory Just Got Unsettlingly Good.
technology.excerpt: Dreaming V3 pushes factual recall from 41 per cent to 83 per cent. Free users are next in line. Privacy hawks are already circling.
technology.image_caption: A 3D-rendered digital brain visualisation representing AI memory and neural networks
technology.nri_angle: India is one of ChatGPT's largest user bases. The new memory system will reach hundreds of millions of Indian users once the free-tier rollout begins. For Indian developers building on the ChatGPT API, persistent memory changes the product design calculus entirely. And the privacy implications land differently in a country with no comprehensive data-protection enforcement yet.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Welcome to 'Chipflation.' AI's Memory Hunger Is Making Your Next Laptop Cost More.
technology.excerpt: DRAM prices doubled in a single quarter. Morgan Stanley says the shortage could last three more years. Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron is one of the biggest winners.
technology.image_caption: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, whose company's stock has nearly quadrupled in 2026
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra is at the epicentre of the memory chip boom. Micron's Gujarat ATMP fab is ramping production. NRI investors holding MU stock have seen it nearly quadruple in 2026. And every Indian American buying a new laptop or phone is about to feel the pinch.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: NVIDIA Is Hiring More H-1B Workers Than Ever. Google and Amazon Are Doing the Opposite.
technology.excerpt: Jensen Huang's chipmaker secured 1,200 visa certifications in six months, up 20 per cent, while Alphabet and Amazon slashed theirs by nearly 40 per cent. For Indian engineers, NVIDIA is now the clearest bet in a tightening market.
technology.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang at a company event in 2025
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers hold 71-73% of all H-1B visas. NVIDIA's hiring surge and top-of-market salaries make it the most critical employer for Indian AI talent, while cutbacks at Google and Amazon narrow the options. The Chip Roy bill threatens the entire pipeline.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Says It Needs $180 Billion to Build a Chip Industry. NITI Aayog Just Published the Roadmap.
technology.excerpt: A new government report targets a $120–150 billion semiconductor value chain by 2035 and admits that 90 to 95 per cent of India's chip demand is currently met by imports. For NRI engineers and investors, it is the most detailed signal yet on where the opportunities lie.
technology.image_caption: Closeup of microchips on a circuit board, the building blocks of the semiconductor industry
technology.nri_angle: Over 50,000 Indian semiconductor professionals work abroad. The roadmap targets compound semiconductors and advanced packaging — skills diaspora engineers have built at TSMC, Intel, and Broadcom. Investment opportunities are emerging in India's chip design startup ecosystem, which raised $92M in five months.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
